text:
Amy - sales: FYI AcmeSec confirmed they want Redwood Private in their VPC for the POC but they mandate outbound TLS inspection. Can we run through options so I can tell them what breaks and what compromises we need?

Sandeep - solutions: TL;DR: TLS-bump will terminate client TLS. Two pain points: 1) original client source IP is replaced by proxy IP (affects per-user billing if you rely on src IP), 2) cert pinning / mutual TLS to model endpoints may fail.

Olivia - netops: Deployment options we can offer:
- Option A: Customer proxy in front, they give us a static allowlist of their proxy EIP(s). We accept traffic from proxy. No src-ip preservation unless they add X-Forwarded-For / PROXY protocol.
- Option B: VPC Peering/Transit: we peer into customer VPC; customer keeps NAT/EIP and we egress via their NAT (src IP preserved as their NAT IP). No TLS inspect on that path.
- Option C: Run a tiny forward-proxy container in their VPC (managed by us) with an assigned EIP so we control egress and can attach billing metadata.

Jordan - eng: Important caveats: if they inspect TLS and re-sign certs, any mTLS or cert pinning from our side will fail unless we exchange CA cert and adjust verification. For artifact pulls (S3/GCS) prefer direct allowlist to their S3 endpoints or pre-stage images in their environment. Also watch websocket MTU issues over tunnel + inspect.

Marta - security: For the GRC questionnaire they asked about key management and audit logs. Quick blurb they can paste: 
"Redwood Private (POC) 4: Customer isolated VPC for data plane. Customer retains control of network egress and firewall rules. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and offers HSM-backed key options on enterprise plans. Built-in request-level audit logs and trace IDs are available via Console; retention configurable to meet compliance needs."

Amy - sales: Great. Can we also give them a minimal firewall/allowlist snippet to hand to their network team? Keep it tight for a POC.

Sandeep - solutions: POC allowlist (recommended):
- TCP 443 -> Redwood control plane + model APIs
- TCP 5222,5223 or TCP 5228-5240 -> streaming/gRPC paths (if using streaming)
- UDP 123 -> NTP (optional if they block time sync)
- TCP/UDP 53 -> DNS (or provide conditional forwarder)
- HTTPS endpoints for artifact registries (S3/GCS) e.g., s3.amazonaws.com, storage.googleapis.com or our artifact mirror
Note: If they use a TLS-inspect proxy, ask them to allow SNI passthrough or not to rewrite SNI.

Olivia - netops: If they want src IP for billing, ask whether their proxy supports PROXY protocol v1/v2 or adding X-Forwarded-For reliably. We can accept PROXY protocol on our connector and capture original IPs into logs, but that requires the proxy to be upstream and not re-NAT after insertion.

Jordan - eng: Also flag: if they require TLS inspection for egress, they must either: 1) accept that model server mTLS/pinning will be disabled, or 2) provide us with their CA cert and sign our endpoint cert chain for the session so we can continue to validate pinned certs. Both have compliance implications.

Marta - security: Small addition for GRC: "Audit logs include request id, timestamp, model id, route, and token hash; logs can be exported to customer SIEM via S3/secure syslog."

support-bot: Created ticket POC-7834 and attached this convo.

Amy - sales: Perfect. I'll send this to AcmeSec. Plan: ask whether they can enable PROXY protocol or XFF, and whether they can allow direct egress for model pulls. I'll update POC-7834 with their response. :raised_hands:
